title: Malayalam Hits Now Earn a Second Box Office From Diaspora Audiences
excerpt: Bethlehem Kudumba Unit's ₹136.5 crore overseas gross and record $1.49 million US run show Malayalam cinema's biggest hits are now bankrolled as much abroad as at home.
body:
• Malayalam cinema’s recent hits now collect a second, diaspora box office: Bethlehem Kudumba Unit grossed ₹136.5 crore overseas against ₹176.88 crore in India gross at the 26-day mark, according to Koimoi trade figures.
  • In the United States, Bethlehem Kudumba Unit finished as the highest-grossing Malayalam film ever with $1.49 million, ahead of L2: Empuraan’s $1.41 million; its North America total was $2.47 million including Canada’s $974,000.
  • The pattern repeats across the industry’s top earners — Lokah: Chapter 1 - Chandra (₹305.17 crore worldwide), Vaazha 2 (₹238.46 crore) and Thudarum (₹237.76 crore) all sit far above their Kerala base in worldwide totals.
  • For diaspora viewers, Bethlehem Kudumba Unit has already made the trip home: it is streaming on JioHotstar after recording 5.4 million views in its opening OTT weekend.

Malayalam cinema is a small industry with a home market of one state. Its biggest films, however, are no longer financed by Kerala alone. Trade figures for the industry’s recent hits show overseas audiences — the Gulf, North America, Europe and Australia — contributing collections on a scale that rivals what the films earn at home, turning the diaspora into a second box office that producers now plan around.

The record that makes the point

The clearest case is Bethlehem Kudumba Unit, the Malayalam romantic comedy-drama directed by Girish AD and starring Nivin Pauly and Mamitha Baiju. Produced by Fahadh Faasil, Dileesh Pothan and Syam Pushkaran under Fahadh Faasil and Friends, Bhavana Studios and Working Class Hero on a reported budget of ₹30 crore, the film had grossed ₹313.38 crore worldwide after 26 days — ₹176.88 crore gross in India and ₹136.5 crore overseas, Koimoi reported. Koimoi’s verdict table, updated November 19, puts its worldwide total higher still, at ₹333.09 crore against ₹164.95 crore from India. Box-office figures are trade estimates; Koimoi notes its numbers are based on estimates and various sources and have not been independently verified.

In the United States, the film became the highest-grossing Malayalam film of all time. It earned $1.44 million in its first 25 days, passing Mohanlal’s L2: Empuraan at $1.41 million, and closed its seven-week North American run at $2.47 million — $1.49 million in the United States and $974,000 in Canada — according to Zoom TV’s closing report. Koimoi attributed the run to word of mouth across North America, Europe, the Middle East and Australia.

Not one film — a pattern across the top of the chart

Bethlehem Kudumba Unit is the latest example, not the only one. Koimoi’s Malayalam verdict table lists Lokah: Chapter 1 - Chandra, the 2025 superhero film starring Kalyani Priyadarshan, at ₹305.17 crore worldwide against ₹157.01 crore in India; Vaazha 2 at ₹238.46 crore worldwide against ₹129.42 crore in India; Mohanlal’s Thudarum at ₹237.76 crore worldwide against ₹122 crore in India; and Drishyam 3 at ₹241.92 crore worldwide against ₹110.36 crore in India. In the United States specifically, the all-time Malayalam chart is now headed by diaspora-driven runs: Bethlehem Kudumba Unit ($1.49 million), L2: Empuraan ($1.41 million), Drishyam 3 ($1.31 million), Lokah: Chapter 1 ($1.26 million) and Manjummel Boys ($1.12 million).

What it means for viewers abroad

For Malayali audiences in the Gulf, the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom, the shift is practical as much as symbolic: overseas performance at this level is what justifies wide simultaneous releases, longer theatrical runs and premium screens far from Kerala. The afterlife is diaspora-shaped too. Bethlehem Kudumba Unit is now streaming on JioHotstar, where it recorded 5.4 million views during its opening weekend on OTT in 2026, ranking as the most-watched non-Hindi Indian film in India at that time, Zoom TV reported. An industry that once treated overseas as a bonus now opens there like it matters — because, on these numbers, it does.

nri_angle: The story is the diaspora itself: Malayali audiences in the Gulf, North America and Europe now deliver collections rivalling the Kerala market for Malayalam cinema's biggest hits.
